children: Walmart Inc. (WMT, Financials), the world's largest retailer, is aiming to transform the image shoppers associate with its clothes aisles.

The company created a fashion pop-up in New York City to coincide with New York Fashion Week, showcasing private labels including Free Assembly and Scoop to a more fashion-forward crowd. It may sound like a branding exercise. There's more to this.

Walmart has spent years growing its grocery business and winning over higher-income shoppers. Apparel provides it a second chance: to convince the same people to spend more once they're already in the shop or app.
The New York event will also highlight Avia, the debut of Walmart's new modern-bohemian label, Scenario, and new designs from designer Brandon Maxwell.

Prices are still firmly on the Walmart side. The pop-up includes some Free Assembly pieces, such a cashmere jumper for $45 and fleece items for $28. The plan is straightforward. Maintain the value buyers expect, but make the clothes feel less like an afterthought.
That's important because clothes and private-label products help build customer loyalty, while providing Walmart more control of assortment and pricing.

The true test for investors will come after Fashion Week. If buyers start to think of Walmart as a destination for clothing, rather than just a place to buy clothes when they shop for groceries, the firm might create another avenue to increase spend per client.

title: Walmart Just Made a Move That Could Change How Millions of Shoppers See It
